question: What is the unified decision for new capital and the held Schwab position in UNH as of November 20, 2026?

epigraph.quote: Respect a breached stop first; a great business in a Stage 4 downtrend will still be there after it builds a base.
epigraph.author: Institutional Research Desk

web_blocks.html: Dual Decision Summary: New capital is REJECTED (TIER_0). Our held Schwab stake of 4.6973 shares carries EXIT_IMMEDIATELY at the November 20 close of $339.85 (TV: $339.88). Selling all 4.6973 shares realizes ~$1,596.38, locking in -$157.56 (-8.98%) against the $1,753.94 cost basis. Directing 100% of proceeds into USD cash lifts U.S. cash from 3.38% ($2,540.35) toward 5.51% inside a 22.0%-floor market Downtrend.

Why Fundamentals and Tape Diverged: Pass 1 reaffirmed UNH's COMPOUNDER_PASS moat [7, 29]. Nine-month 2026 revenue hit $336.45B, EBIT rose 27% to $23.54B, and CFO climbed 35% to $25.09B [7, 29]. At $339.85, UNH trades at 14.50x forward P/E and prices in just 3.15% annual FCFE growth. Yet Q3 2026 footnotes expose $1.77B of reserve releases, $133.35B of goodwill and intangibles (42.6% of assets), and $74.33B of debt [29]. All three credit agencies hold Negative outlooks while parent cash sits at $1.2B [29]. Unresolved DOJ FCA suits and March 2026 IRS transfer-pricing NOPAs add tail risk [29]. Last week's -16.67% drop into STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) broke both our $365.05 alert and $358.00 stop, forcing an immediate exit.

web_blocks.title: How Prior Assumptions Changed Since November 17, 2026
paragraphs: On November 17, the prior dossier rated UNH WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT with a $365.30–$376.42 band, $358.00 stop, and $465.00 target at 0 shares. Schwab then bought 4.6973 shares at $373.39 average on November 16–18 before UNH crashed -16.67% to $339.85. Meanwhile, our Q3 2026 10-Q audit exposed $1.77B in reserve releases, Optum Health Q3 margin cooling to 3.2%, March 2026 IRS NOPAs, and three Negative credit outlooks [29]. Re-underwriting cuts the risk-adjusted base target to $365.00 ($352.00 expected value, +3.6%), sets new capital to REJECTED (TIER_0), and triggers an immediate exit.

book_paragraphs: Every great investment framework separates what a company can earn over a decade from what its stock price is telling you right now. On November 20, 2026, UnitedHealth Group delivers a textbook lesson in why that separation saves real money. Operationally, UnitedHealth Group remains the largest and most deeply integrated healthcare franchise in the United States, serving 48.3 million medical members through UnitedHealthcare and generating $25.09 billion in operating cash flow across the first nine months of 2026. Yet in the span of a single week ending November 20, the stock fell 16.67 percent to close at $339.85 on more than twice average daily volume, shattering its 50-day, 200-day, and 30-week moving averages.

For new capital, our verdict is REJECTED at Tier 0 conviction. We never allocate fresh funds to a stock in a confirmed Stage 4 decline inside a 10-distribution-day U.S. market downtrend, regardless of how low its 14.50 times forward price-to-earnings ratio appears. For the existing portfolio position of 4.6973 shares held in Charles Schwab—worth $1,596.38 against a $1,753.94 cost basis—our verdict is EXIT IMMEDIATELY. Those shares breached our prior $358.00 structural invalidation stop by more than 5 percent. Selling all 4.6973 shares and holding 100 percent of the proceeds in USD cash protects capital and begins repairing a U.S. portfolio cash reserve that sat at a critically low 3.38 percent against a 22.0 percent Downtrend target.

book_subsections.title: What Changed Between the Prior Dossier and Today
paragraphs: Three developments since the November 17, 2026 monograph transformed the risk picture. First, our verdict-blind audit of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q and 2026 proxy filings uncovered meaningful caveats beneath the headline earnings rebound. Reported medical costs in the first nine months of 2026 benefited from $1.44 billion in favorable prior-year reserve releases and $331 million in loss-contract releases, while management explicitly warned in MD&A that CMS's finalized 2.48 percent Medicare Advantage rate update for 2027 still lags medical cost inflation.

Second, footnote forensics revealed heavier balance-sheet and enforcement friction than earlier chapters captured: $133.35 billion in goodwill and net intangibles against $104.13 billion of equity, $74.33 billion of consolidated debt carrying Negative credit outlooks from Moody's, S&P, and Fitch with just $1.2 billion in unrestricted parent cash, Optum Health's Q3 margin slipping to 3.2 percent, unresolved DOJ Medicare billing litigation, and March 6, 2026 IRS transfer-pricing Notices of Proposed Adjustment for 2017 through 2020. Incorporating a 50-basis-point credit premium (10.0 percent Ke) and a $4.0 billion ($4.46 per share) legal reserve reduced our 12-month risk-adjusted base-case intrinsic value from $465.00 to $365.00 per share ($352.00 probability-weighted expected value, or +3.6 percent—below ~4.76 percent U.S. Treasury yields).

Third, the stock's price action broke every near-term support floor. While our market-facts ledger still tags UNH as Stage 1 Basing, the live TradingView snapshot places UNH squarely in Stage 4 below its $388.70 50-day average and $368.54 200-day average, with no upward 4-hour reversal turn and illiquid options spreads. Applying the stricter Stage 4 rule keeps us out of harm's way while waiting for a genuine Stage 1 base to form in the $300.00 to $325.00 range.

Finally, our capital redeployment review compared holding cash against rotating immediately into either shortlist biopharma leader Eli Lilly or managed-care peer Elevance Health. Elevance Health also sits in Stage 4 at $394.48, making a sector peer swap counterproductive. Eli Lilly holds Stage 2 leadership at $1,347.11, yet trades above its $1,282.61 to $1,321.67 support band inside a 10-distribution-day U.S. Downtrend. Directing 100 percent of UNH exit proceeds into USD cash strengthens portfolio liquidity from 3.38 percent toward 5.51 percent and preserves optionality until market breadth heals.

book_subsections.title: How to Use This Monograph as an Owner or Observer
paragraphs: Chapters 1 through 6 walk step-by-step through UnitedHealth Group's fifty-year evolution from a regional HMO into a $448 billion integrated payer-and-services giant, its six operating engines across UnitedHealthcare and Optum, its per-$100 revenue unit economics, regulatory moat pressures, management walk-the-talk scorecard, and ten-year cash conversion forensics. Chapters 7 through 9 then pair that price-blind foundation with live Reverse DCF valuation, multi-timeframe technical structure, and our two-sided capital decision. Even while new capital stays at zero percent today, understanding the underlying business mechanics prepares you to act decisively if and when a genuine Stage 1 base matures into a fresh Stage 2 uptrend.

book_subsections.title: What Our Six-Vector Blind-Spot Audit Uncovered
paragraphs: A companion dossier refresh exists specifically to catch blind spots that earlier reports overlooked. Across all six investigative vectors—customer concentration, footnote balance-sheet forensics, hidden unit-economics friction, adjacent non-listed competition, tax and currency exposure, and governance incentives—this refresh surfaced material disclosures from the 2025 Form 10-K, 2026 proxy filings, and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q. First, CMS premium revenues climbed to 44 percent of total consolidated revenues, while 60.3 percent of Optum's nine-month 2026 revenue came from affiliated UnitedHealthcare contracts, explaining why UHC membership pruning also reduced Optum Rx prescription volume.

Second, adjacent unlisted disruptors—including transparent flat-fee pharmacy benefit managers like Cost Plus Drugs and Capital Rx, direct-to-consumer pharma cash channels, private-equity-backed value-based care enablers, and multi-clearinghouse revenue-cycle rivals—help explain Optum Rx's decision to shift toward 100 percent manufacturer rebate pass-through by January 2028. Third, proxy and 8-K filings highlighted governance tensions worth watching: 20.24 percent shareholder support for an independent board chair, Stephen Hemsley's $60 million cliff-vesting option grant following 2025 Say-on-Pay pushback, the appointment of former Deloitte partner Dennis Stankiewicz as Chief Accounting Officer at a firm audited by Deloitte since 2002, and $964 million in cumulative currency translation losses sitting inside South American assets held for sale. Putting all of those pieces beside a broken Stage 4 chart makes capital preservation the obvious priority today.

In short, our November 20, 2026 audit balances respect for UnitedHealth Group's unmatched operating scale against strict financial and technical discipline. Exiting all 4.6973 Charles Schwab shares at $339.85 respects the breached $358.00 structural stop, raises portfolio cash from 3.38 percent toward 5.51 percent inside a 10-distribution-day market downtrend, and avoids catching a falling knife while Managed Care peers Elevance Health and Cigna remain trapped in Stage 4 declines. Meanwhile, placing UNH on a monitor-only watch around $300.00 to $325.00 keeps the franchise ready for unbiased re-underwriting the moment a genuine Stage 1 base matures and reclaims rising 50-day and 30-week averages.

book_callouts.title: Two Questions Every Dossier Must Answer Separately
book_callouts.text: First, is this a strong underlying business? Yes—UNH earns COMPOUNDER_PASS on long-term cash conversion and scale. Second, is this the right day and price structure to risk capital? No—a Stage 4 stop breach with unresolved tax and rating overhangs requires exiting immediately and waiting in cash.
